Other operations configure idle scanning, update boot-sequence information or force a group-key refresh. Functions are resolved from the driver library, so the player-side API is separate from the chipset-specific implementation and the diagnostic files exposed by that driver.
primitives.wifi_sonosnet: Manages wireless settings and coordinated SonosNet channel changes, with the network-start daemon applying the requested configuration. The state includes the wireless mode, frequency, enable status and wired-network condition. Before a change that could disconnect the controller, the player records recovery information; if controller confirmation does not arrive, it can re-enable wireless operation or revert the change. Channel-change messages coordinate a later channel hop with other players. These recovery and coordination steps are separate from saving an SSID and password.
primitives.assoctracker: Measures how a phone or other controller discovers the speaker and starts communicating with it. For each controller IP address, it records discovery searches and reply failures, whether the local network resolved the controller's hardware address, requests for the speaker's description and zone state, and subsequent group notifications. It keeps at most four records. A record becomes eligible for expiration after 30 seconds from its first discovery request and is cleared on the next sweep. A qualifying record becomes a CrAssoc connection-health report containing the observed times, attempt counts and errors. Later activity does not extend the window, and expiration clears the record even if the reporting channel does not accept it.
primitives.arping: Checks a local-network IP address by scheduling address-resolution probes. A caller supplies the probe timing and arms the ARP manager; its worker performs the network work rather than making the caller run the probe synchronously. The manager retains probe results and pending-reset state, which the requesting monitor can read on a later cycle. That monitor then decides whether to retry or reset its connection. The remaining probe-result and caller-policy details stay open in the technical record.
primitives.netsettings_mgr: Owns the saved network configuration and pushes changes to the network-start daemon for application. Its operations include incrementing the configuration version and rotating network keys, with diagnostic JSON or text views of the current settings. Applying a new configuration is a separate step from storing it. Failed updates can enter automatic-revert handling, and failure of that recovery is reported explicitly, so a successful settings write alone does not prove the new network connection is working.
primitives.mdp_flash: Reads manufacturing data pages from flash storage, including the player's serial identity and calibration information. Sonos and flash libraries expose the original and second-page forms, serial-number conversion, page version information and write operations. This data is separate from ordinary room names and user preferences stored in the settings directory. The record identifies the factory-data access layer; individual field layouts and write permissions belong to the relevant page and accessor implementations.
primitives.mod_zp: Provides the application-level zone-player module and its background worker pools. The module includes player and service-account components and a related album-art module. Shutdown is ordered: it stops HTTP and player work, modern-API and event workers, resets zone-related state, and releases timed-job and thread-pool resources. This ordering helps explain why stopping the program requires more than dropping one playback object. The module inventory does not itself define a new client command.
primitives.rmd_op_worker_class: The RMD worker class: a worker-object family in the remote-diagnostics machinery, where operations run as discrete work items.
primitives.timedjobs: The timed-jobs registry: the scheduled-task table, covering which periodic jobs exist and when they run.
primitives.timers: The timer machinery: the scheduling primitives, covering how work gets deferred and periodic jobs fire.
primitives.dropout_logging: Dropout logging: it detects and records audio playback gaps, providing the data behind 'the music keeps cutting out' diagnostics by noting where and when gaps happened.
primitives.tls_stack: The TLS stack: the secure-connection machinery covering certificates, handshakes, and the encrypted channel everything secure uses.
primitives.entitlements: The entitlements data: which features this unit or household is licensed for, which is the record behind feature gating and the machinery deciding what this unit is entitled to do.
primitives.audiotap: Copies audio from selected processing locations into diagnostic captures, for example the DSP output or the TV's digital input. The tap manager normally allows two simultaneous locations, rejects duplicate names and refuses locations whose source does not permit capture; its three physical slots allow a configured maximum of three. A separate SPDIF recorder keeps up to 25 MB of recent input. Taking its snapshot removes captured bytes from the rolling buffer and writes a zlib-compressed file. Exporting wraps that file in base64 text inside an XML element and then deletes it, so the same saved snapshot cannot be exported repeatedly.
primitives.location: The location feature: the machinery for household 'locations', which is per-place configuration inside the settings model.
primitives.albumart_proxy: The album-art proxy: it serves artwork through the player's own web server so apps load covers from the speaker rather than fetching them remotely each time. This is why artwork in the app loads fast and keeps working offline.
primitives.muse_route_verbs: The modern-API route verbs: the operation-name vocabulary bound to routes, covering every verb the API can invoke.
primitives.accepted_mimes: The complete list of audio formats the player accepts: every content type it will actually try to play, from FLAC and MP3 through AAC and Ogg variants. This is the real 'what can it play' list, recovered verbatim from the binary's accept table.
primitives.aha_ops: Operations for a legacy partner integration called 'aha': present in the shared codebase as part of the service-integration layer, recovered as a named operation family.
primitives.auto_update_policy: The auto-update policy: the rules deciding when and whether the household may update itself, covering timing windows, opt-in state, and rollout conditions. It's why a fleet of speakers updates overnight by itself.
primitives.avt_session: The transport session object: the per-playback-session state the transport engine keeps, covering source, position, and mode for whatever's playing. Every playing thing gets one.
primitives.boot_reasons: Boot-reason tracking: it records why the player started, distinguishing cold power-on, reboot after update, crash recovery, and watchdog trips. It powers the 'why did my speaker reboot' answer diagnostics give.
primitives.browse_categories: The library's browse categories: the top-level groupings the music index offers like artists, albums, genres, playlists, and folders. These are the fixed shelves of the library tree every browse starts from.
primitives.channel_source_types: The channel-source type vocabulary: the kinds of audio channels the system models, deciding who plays left, who plays right, and who carries the low end in a bonded rig.
primitives.chirp_sdk: The chirp SDK interface: the internal API for the speaker-identification tone, covering start, stop, and configure. It gives the room-detection commands one shared interface for identification sounds.
primitives.config_parsers: The configuration parsers: the readers for each config file and document format the system loads, mapping which parser owns which file.
primitives.ddthrd: An internal thread or component by build-tree naming: recovered structurally as part of the program's worker modules.
primitives.dev_unlock: The device-unlock flag path: the gated marker controlling whether restricted functions are permitted on this unit. It's deliberately gated because unlocking widens what the unit will do.
primitives.diag_instructions: The diagnostics-instructions flow: how the player fetches instructions from Sonos about what diagnostic data to gather and where to send it, which is the guided-support machinery behind a support session.
primitives.diagnostics_submit: Diagnostics submission: the packaging and sending of a support bundle, covering how 'submit diagnostics' gathers everything and ships it with its tracking ID.
primitives.didl_escaping: Metadata escaping rules: how special characters inside track metadata are encoded so the document stays valid. It's the detail that keeps a title containing '&' or '<' from breaking the metadata document.
primitives.dsp_drc: The signal-processing dynamic-range control: the stage that compresses the loud/quiet range, behind night-mode and loudness-management behaviors.
primitives.ducking_engine: The ducking engine: the logic that lowers music when something more important plays, which is how alerts and voice responses sit on top without fully stopping the music. The level dips for the alert's duration.
primitives.enum_tables: The enumeration tables: the named-constant vocabularies recovered across the firmware, covering the states, modes, and codes internal machinery speaks.
primitives.ext_audio_source: External audio sources: the machinery for audio arriving outside the normal playback path, covering the line-in family and external feeds that enter through this layer into the playback pipeline.
primitives.group_capabilities: Group capability flags: what a group can do as a unit, meaning capabilities that only make sense or only become available once speakers are grouped.
primitives.healthcheck_job: The healthcheck job: the scheduled task that actually runs the periodic self-test on its timer.
primitives.http_request_security: HTTP request security: the checks applied to incoming web requests, covering validation and restrictions protecting the web surface.
primitives.httpcache_manager: The HTTP cache manager: the component owning the web-content cache, covering what's stored, eviction, and freshness policies.
primitives.ibt_engine: The IBT engine: an internal data-movement component identified by build-tree naming, recovered structurally.
primitives.idle_shutdown_reasons: Idle shutdown reasons: the vocabulary of why an idle system stopped or slept, distinguishing timeouts, policies, and commanded shutdowns.
primitives.inprocess_events: In-process events: the internal publish-and-subscribe inside this program, which is how one component notifies another without network involvement.
primitives.lechmere_cmds: The lechmere command vocabulary: the command set of the websocket and eventing layer, meaning what messages the modern event channel carries.
primitives.location_settings_sync: Location settings sync: it keeps location-based configuration synchronized across the household, part of the per-location settings feature.
primitives.mdns_stack: Speakers advertise their identity, addresses, secure ports and API paths through a local _sonos._tcp. service. An address refresh that skips full rebinding increases the sequence and rebuilds the advertisement, including unchanged-address notifications. Initial address acquisition and permitted rebinding do not increase it. Ordinary TXT updates skip duplicates, and receiving players do not enforce increasing sequence numbers.
primitives.misc_components: Miscellaneous components: the assorted internal modules that don't warrant their own entry, inventoried for completeness.
primitives.misc_health: Miscellaneous health checks: additional self-test points beyond the main periodic healthcheck job.
primitives.misc_mgrs: Miscellaneous managers: the leftover *Mgr-named components of the architecture, recovered structurally to complete the inventory.
primitives.muse_grouping_ops: The modern-API grouping operations: the route-level machinery for group management in the JSON surface.
primitives.muse_network_test: The modern-API network-test operations: the connectivity-probing routes, which are the routes behind network diagnostics from the JSON surface.
primitives.muse_upnp_bridge_actions: The bridge operations: modern-API verbs that reach through to the classic command layer, which is how the JSON surface drives the old services like stereo pairing and satellites.
primitives.netif_events: Network-interface events: the events fired when interfaces change state, carrying link health and signal strength per interface.
primitives.netstart_ipc: The network-startup IPC: the internal message channel to the network-startup machinery, which is how this program coordinates with the process bringing up networking.
primitives.nodetx_transport: The nodetx transport: the transport for node-level telemetry messages between players, which is the wire the household health traffic travels.
primitives.ota_update: Over-the-air update: the update-download machinery, which fetches new firmware packages from the update channel.
primitives.ota_upgrade: The OTA upgrade path: applying a downloaded update, which is the install-and-reboot sequence that puts the new firmware live.
primitives.platform_details: Platform details: hardware and platform-specific facts the code consults, covering the model and board-level particulars recovered.
primitives.rate_limiter: The rate limiter: it throttles repeated operations, guarding against a client flooding the player with requests.
primitives.rincon_didl_fields: The Sonos-specific metadata fields: the extension vocabulary in track metadata covering radio names, track gains, chapter numbers, and other fields beyond the standard set.
primitives.rincon_uuid: The rincon UUID scheme: how Sonos device identifiers are formed, which is the 'RINCON_' ID family naming players and households.
primitives.settings_xml: The settings XML formats: the document grammars for stored configuration, covering how settings are serialized on disk and wire.
primitives.smapi_jwt: SMAPI JWT handling: the token format and verification for music-service authentication, which is how service credentials are validated.
primitives.smapi_layer: The SMAPI layer: the Sonos Music API machinery as a whole, which is the common interface over the many music services the player talks to.
primitives.smb_shares: SMB share handling: the Windows-file-sharing client for music libraries, covering dialect negotiation and folder access for NAS shares.
primitives.sonarcal: The sonar-calibration machinery: this generation's room tuning, which is the measure-tone-analyze-adjust flow that predates the Trueplay branding.
primitives.speaker_group_advertise: Speaker-group advertisement: how a player announces its group role to the household, whether coordinator or member.
primitives.ssh_authorized_keys: The SSH keys surface: authorized-key management on the web surface for installing and removing keys, which is a security-relevant access path documented explicitly.
primitives.stream_error_counters: Stream error counters: tallies of streaming failures, which are the numbers the stream-diagnostics pages show for radio and HTTP playback.
primitives.telemetry_endpoints: The telemetry endpoints: the collection addresses where usage and health data is sent.
primitives.timezone_table: The timezone table: the firmware's internal timezone list, which is the zones the time-zone commands index into.
primitives.tsclient: The 'tsclient' component: an internal client module by build-tree naming, recovered structurally.
primitives.txst_enum: The 'txst' enumeration: a named-constant vocabulary in the transmit and state machinery, recovered as constants.
primitives.uri_service_map: The URI-to-service map: which address schemes route to which playing implementation, which is the key that turns 'what kind of item is this' into 'who plays it'. It's the routing table behind every x-sonos and x-rincon address.
primitives.vli_grouping: VLI grouping: how virtual line-in sessions relate to groups, covering whether a pushed-audio session follows group membership.
primitives.vli_playback_tracker: The VLI playback tracker: it monitors a virtual line-in session's playback state, tracking the external feed's lifecycle.
primitives.vli_transport_detail: VLI transport internals: the details of how pushed audio travels in a virtual line-in session, covering the transport-side machinery.
primitives.wakelock_guard: The wakelock guard: it prevents the device from sleeping while critical work runs, which is the 'don't sleep during playback or update' safeguard.
primitives.watchdog_crash: The watchdog crash path: what happens when the watchdog fires, covering logging the unresponsive state, rebooting, and reporting the trip so crashes get diagnosed.
primitives.websocket_server: The websocket server: the endpoint accepting websocket connections, which is the server side of the modern event channel.
primitives.wifi_idle_roles: WiFi idle roles: the low-power wireless states, covering how the radio behaves when the player is idle.
primitives.action_dispatch_records: How each service looks up your command: a sorted name table that gets binary-searched, each entry pairing a command name with the routine that runs it. The authoritative list behind which commands each service can execute.
primitives.service_impl_vtables: The service implementation tables: how the object-based services wire commands to the routines that run them, showing which services route through implementation objects and how.
primitives.dirobj_class_map: The directory-object class map: the internal inventory of container and object classes the library uses, which is how folders, playlists, and items are typed in the index.
primitives.binary_section_map: Where the program's data physically lives: which program sections hold which tables, so every referenced table is anchored to a real location in the binary. It's what makes every documented structure verifiable rather than claimed.
primitives.protobuf_descriptors: The protobuf descriptors: 103 embedded message schemas fully decoded field by field, which is the structured-data format the modern layers use, recovered into a complete wire grammar.

uri_formats.x-rincon-queue: How you address the local play queue. When a command says 'play the queue' or 'play track 5 of the queue', the address it hands the player starts with x-rincon-queue: followed by the player's own ID. The address identifies the queue itself rather than an item inside it, and a '#5' style suffix on some forms pins it to a specific queue position.
uri_formats.sonos_queue_track_uri: How a queue-track reference looks when the player emits one: the device-and-queue address plus a fragment naming the track's position. It lets a reply identify exactly which entry is meant rather than just 'the queue'.
uri_formats.x-rincon-stream: How you point a player at another room's audio. When rooms are grouped, the followers don't fetch the music themselves; they play a stream served by the group leader, and this address names that stream using the source player's ID plus a stream reference. It's the address that makes 'play what the living room is playing' work across the network.
uri_formats.x-rincon-mp3radio: The address family for internet radio. A radio-station item carries this scheme so the player knows it's a live MP3 stream to tune into rather than a file or queue entry. It's the marker that sends the request down the streaming-radio path.
uri_formats.x-rincon-playlist: The address of a saved Sonos playlist, which is how commands refer to a stored playlist rather than the live queue. Handing this scheme to 'play' loads the playlist as the current source.
uri_formats.x-rincon-cpcontainer: How a music service's browsable folders are addressed. When an app browses a service's catalog (its playlists, charts, and stations), the containers it walks carry addresses in this scheme, tagging them as provider-hosted content rather than local items.
uri_formats.x-rincon-buzzer: The address of the player's built-in alarm tones. Instead of waking to music, an alarm can play a buzzer sound stored inside the speaker's own software, and this scheme names those built-in assets so an alarm's 'sound' can be something that works with zero network. These files live inside the speaker itself, so there's nothing for you to download or configure.
uri_formats.x-rincon-sonarcal: The addresses of the sonar-calibration audio: the test tones played during this generation's room-tuning process, including the leader tone, the test tone, and the completion sound. They are kept as built-in assets inside the player rather than files on your network.
uri_formats.x-rincon-configmode-sonar: The addresses of the setup and calibration tones: the chirps and test sounds the player emits during speaker-detection and room-calibration. These point at built-in audio files used while configuring a system, not at music, and they live inside the speaker where you never interact with them directly.
uri_formats.x-sonos-vli: The address of a virtual line-in source, the marker for audio being pushed at the player by an external feed rather than pulled from a queue or stream. Seeing this scheme means the sound originates outside the normal playback machinery.
uri_formats.x-sonos-misc: A catch-all of internal Sonos address schemes for odds and ends: home-theater audio streams, plain HTTP variants, MMS-era stream types, service locators. Individually rare, collectively the long tail of sources the player can address.
uri_formats.x-sonosapi-*: The address family for cloud and music-service items: the whole family of schemes that say 'this item lives behind a service's API', covering HLS streams, radio services, and streaming-service tracks. Each variant marks how the player should fetch and interpret the content.
uri_formats.x-sonosapi-radio: The address of a Sonos Radio station. It carries the station identifier plus flags and a session number as parameters, and pairs with an API-key header when the station is fetched.
uri_formats.spotify_scheme: Spotify's own address family: 'spotify:track:' and friends plus the x-spotify form. These are the markers telling the player an item comes through the Spotify integration rather than the generic service path, so the request routes through the Spotify machinery.
uri_formats.explore_scheme: The 'explore:' container scheme, an address family for explorable content collections that sits alongside the radio and container schemes. It marks browsable sections of service catalogs rather than individual playable items.
uri_formats.rdradio_scheme: The 'rdradio:' scheme, an address family marking radio-station items for the streaming-radio path. It's how a saved station is identified as something to tune into rather than a file to fetch.
uri_formats.hls_radio: An HLS-radio stream variant, meaning Apple's segmented-stream format used for radio. The tag in the address tells the player to pick the right streaming machinery for it.
uri_formats.hls_aac: An HLS variant in AAC encoding: a segmented-stream address whose marker steers the fetch machinery toward the right decoder for that format.
uri_formats.hm_scheme: The 'hm://' address for the Spotify Connect channel. It routes to the embedded Spotify component (the 'Hermes' path) that lets the speaker appear as a Spotify Connect device in the Spotify app.
uri_formats.pndrradioad: Pandora's ad-insertion stream marker: the address variant used when Pandora injects ads into a stream. It lets the player treat those segments correctly rather than mistaking them for the station's audio.
uri_formats.skd: A scheme token present in the streamer's vocabulary whose meaning couldn't be resolved. It's recorded for completeness with the honest note that its purpose is unknown rather than guessing.
uri_formats.stub_scheme: A stub scheme token, most likely a placeholder marking a source the player recognizes but can't actually play. It stands in where a real address would go.
uri_formats.misc_schemes: Address schemes missed by the main sweep: oddballs like Pandora's ad-insertion transport and HLS radio variants. They're collected so the scheme inventory is genuinely complete rather than just the common cases.
uri_formats.protocol_info_schemes: The scheme vocabulary the player advertises in its capability strings: the address families it tells the world it can accept or produce. Devices read them when checking compatibility before handing each other streams.
uri_formats.sonos_albumart_path: The filename pattern for album-art assets the player stores or serves. It's a GUID-shaped name so every image has a unique, stable address that apps can cache against.
uri_formats.sonos_settings_rest: The settings paths the player calls on the household's configuration service, which is where effective settings and per-location settings live on the REST surface.
uri_formats.http-endpoints-muse: The outbound API paths the player itself calls. When the player acts as a client toward other players or the cloud, these are the route templates it formats its requests against.
uri_formats.cloud_api_routes: The full map of outbound cloud API calls the player can make: hundreds of route templates covering everything the player asks Sonos's cloud for, including accounts, services, updates, and telemetry. It's documented as the outbound counterpart of the API the player serves.
uri_formats.rinconnetworks_urn: The 'RinconNetworks' URN namespace prefix: the internal namespace Sonos's metadata and service identifiers use. 'Rincon' is the platform's internal codename, which is why it appears throughout these schemes.
uri_formats.oauth_jwt_urn: A standard token-grant identifier from the OAuth world. It's part of the vocabulary used when the player exchanges credentials with services, recorded as reference rather than a playable address.
uri_formats.sonos-schemes: Bare 'sonos:' addresses used internally as templates and identifiers, a small family of Sonos-namespaced locators for housekeeping rather than playable content. They show up inside the system's own bookkeeping rather than in anything you'd browse to.
uri_formats.x_rincon_schemes: The x-rincon* scheme family as a group: the queue, radio, buzzer, calibration, and container address types collected under their shared 'rincon' prefix, rincon being Sonos's internal platform name.
uri_formats.x_sonos_schemes: The x-sonos* scheme family as a group: every Sonos-prefixed address type and the headers that travel with them, collected so the whole family's grammar lives in one place.
uri_formats.tqueue_scheme_registry: The complete zoo of playable address schemes harvested from the queue engine's routing table: every scheme the queue knows how to direct, in one inventory. It is the master list of what kinds of source addresses exist.
uri_formats.tqueue_probe_chain: The queue's address-sniffing chain. When a URI arrives that isn't obviously one type, the queue probes it through an ordered fallback sequence to figure out what it actually is.
uri_formats.pndrradio-http: Pandora's plain-HTTP radio variant: the non-ad stream address used for the normal station feed, as distinct from the ad-insertion variant.
uri_formats.hls-radio: An HLS radio stream address: segmented radio appearing in the scheme vocabulary as its own token.
uri_formats.hls-aac: An HLS AAC stream address: segmented AAC audio in the scheme vocabulary, distinct from the generic HLS token.
uri_formats.stub: A stub-player address: the placeholder used where a real source hasn't been selected yet. It's a stand-in address rather than playable content.
uri_formats.hm: The Spotify 'Hermes' channel: the hardware bridge inside the embedded Spotify client that carries Connect traffic. It's what the hm:// addresses route to.
uri_formats.sonos_com-hls-radio: An HLS-radio address carrying the 'sonos.com' service prefix: the service-namespaced form of the segmented-radio scheme, tagging which provider the stream belongs to.
uri_formats.pandora_com-pndrradioad: A Pandora ad-insertion address with the service prefix: Pandora's ad stream with the provider prefix attached, in the service-namespaced form.
uri_formats.last_fm-radio-http: A Last.fm radio HTTP address: the service-namespaced radio scheme for the Last.fm integration, a leftover of one of the older service partnerships.
uri_formats.x-sonos-unknown: The 'unknown source' placeholder: the address the player uses when it can't identify what a source is. It's a safe label rather than a wrong guess.
uri_formats.rhapsody_imageserver: The Rhapsody (later Napster) image-server addresses, describing how artwork from that service's catalog was fetched. It's a leftover of one of Sonos's oldest music-service integrations, kept for compatibility.

payload_formats.didl_lite: The track-metadata format end to end: the XML envelope carrying title, artist, album, artwork, class, and resource for every track the player describes, plus the Sonos-specific extension fields. This is the single most-seen document in the system, because everything 'now playing' passes through it.
payload_formats.didl_lite_header: The opening lines of the track-metadata XML the player emits when describing tracks: the namespace declarations every track description starts with.
payload_formats.didl_res_protocolinfo: How a track's resource line describes its format: the 'protocolInfo' field pattern the player writes per source scheme, declaring the MIME type and addressing each item uses.
payload_formats.didl_cdudn_desc: A special descriptor element in track metadata: the 'cdudn' desc that tags which content directory an item came from. It lets the system trace an item back to its source library.
payload_formats.soap_envelope: The request and response envelope: the wrapping document every command call and reply is built inside, consisting of header, body, and the per-command element naming the operation and its service.
payload_formats.soap_envelope_variants: The two envelope openings the command layer uses: one with an explicit encoding-style declaration and one without. Both wrap the same request and response bodies.
payload_formats.soap_fault_wire: The body of a fault reply: the exact document skeleton every error response is built as, carrying the code and description fields that tell a caller what failed.
payload_formats.soapaction_header: The command-name header: the HTTP header that says which operation a request wants (service type plus action name). It's the routing key telling the player which command to run.
payload_formats.gena_event_envelope: The wire envelope of a classic event notification: the propertyset body plus the headers (event type, sequence number, subscription ID, and Sonos's own boot counter) that make a notification a valid subscription message.
payload_formats.upnp_gena_event_doc: The envelope of a classic event notification: the 'propertyset' document the player sends when it announces changed variables to subscribers, plus the LastChange wrapper for bundled updates.
payload_formats.lastchange_templates: The three LastChange document roots: the envelope shapes each service's bundled-change report uses, with their per-service namespaces. Every service uses one of these roots, and this is the shared shape underneath the per-service details.
payload_formats.sonos_lastchange_attr_form: A Sonos formatting choice worth knowing: the player's LastChange documents write each changed variable as an attribute-valued element rather than the element-body style other devices use. A parser expecting the standard shape will misread these.
payload_formats.protocolinfo: The full capability vocabulary the player declares in its format strings: every MIME type and scheme it claims to send or accept. It's the complete 'what can this box play' contract.
payload_formats.scpd: The service-specification documents: the advertised command lists served at /xml/*.xml, describing what the product claims to support as distinct from what the binary actually implements. This page's whole availability story rests on that comparison.
payload_formats.device_description: The root device-description document: the file every client fetches first, containing the player's self-description with its substitution tokens filled and the list of all 16 service specs it advertises.
payload_formats.sonos_alarm_doc: The alarm document's opening structure: the versioned envelope the stored alarm list is written in, carrying which device last updated it.
payload_formats.savedqueues_rsq: The saved-playlists file format: the structure of the file where Sonos playlists persist, with per-playlist records carrying versioning and track lists. It's written atomically so a crash can't leave a corrupt store.
payload_formats.sonos_saved_queue_file: The saved-playlists filename, 'savedqueues.rsq': the on-disk file where Sonos playlists persist across reboots.
payload_formats.sonos_saved_queue_id: How a saved-playlist ID is written: 'SQ:' followed by a number. It's the identifier commands use to name which stored playlist they mean.
payload_formats.trackqueue_rsq: The live-queue persistence format: how the current play queue is written to disk. It's a transactional store with a guard mechanism so an interrupted write doesn't destroy the queue.
payload_formats.sonos_queue_doc: The 'NumTracks' attribute the queue's XML documents carry, meaning how the queue's track count is written in its stored form.
payload_formats.sonos_track_summary_doc: The track-summary document roots: the envelope the player's queue-summary endpoints emit when describing what's in the queue.
payload_formats.sonos_browse_filter_vocab: Which metadata fields a browse request can ask for: the accepted filter lists (title, artist, album, duration, resource) so callers know what they can select back.
payload_formats.upnp_search_criteria_vocab: The search grammar the library accepts: which 'where' clauses a search request can legally use, namely matching by object class and reference-ID existence.
payload_formats.scrobble_submission: The scrobbling submission format: the form a last.fm-style 'now playing report' takes when the player submits your listening history to a scrobble service, carrying session, artist, title, timestamp, and source per track.
payload_formats.SonosSeekTime: How a seek-time argument is written. When you scrub to a position, the time arrives as text with a specific grammar: an optional minus sign for 'go back', then numbers. The parser is strict enough that the exact accepted shapes were recovered, and this entry documents what the seek argument can legally look like.
payload_formats.SonosTrackOrdinal: How 'play track N' is expressed: the number you send to select a track by position. The parser accepts ordinary decimal text with the usual tolerance for spacing and signs, and this documents what counts as a valid track number.
payload_formats.SonosRcInstance: The instance-number convention on the volume service: the commands expect the instance to be 0 and reject anything else. It uses a different rejection code than the transport service, a quirk worth knowing when an app gets a fault back.
payload_formats.SonosRcChannel: The channel names the volume and tone commands accept: 'Master', 'LF' (left-front), 'RF' (right-front), plus some extended tokens used internally. Sending an unrecognized channel name is an error, so the accepted vocabulary is documented exactly.
payload_formats.sonos_duration_hhmmss: How durations are written: the sleep timer's hours:minutes:seconds format, where 'stop in 20 minutes' travels as 00:20:00. This documents the exact accepted shape of the duration argument.
payload_formats.sonos_iso8601_timestamps: How timestamps are written. Two shapes are accepted: the compact form (20241031T153000.000Z) and the dashed extended form, used wherever times travel in arguments.
payload_formats.sonos_http_date: How the player reads HTTP Date headers. The three date spellings web standards allow are all accepted, so servers writing any of them parse correctly.
payload_formats.sonos_signed_blob_json: The signed-blob envelope: a JSON wrapper carrying a magic marker, a length, a checksum, and a counter. It's used where the player needs a self-verifying data block that can't be silently truncated or corrupted.
payload_formats.group_effective_values_blob: A second signed-blob variant: the version-11 sibling envelope used for group effective-values data, with its own magic marker distinguishing it.
payload_formats.sonos_access_settings_json: The template of the access-control settings document: the small JSON record controlling restricted-admin and read-access levels on the player.
payload_formats.sonos_track_encryption_meta: The track-encryption metadata fields: elements describing how a track's data is encrypted, for the protected content the player can handle.
payload_formats.sonos_state_flags: Zone state flags as written: the 'frozen / allowed / auto' style fields the zone settings carry as packed text rather than separate booleans.
payload_formats.sonos_audio_settings_line: The packed audio-settings line: a compact serialization stuffing every tone and volume setting into one text record, covering volume, balance, bass, treble, loudness, and the surround and sub fields in a fixed order.
payload_formats.sonos_linein_demo: The line-in demo-mode settings field: a bracketed flag the settings store carries for the line-in feature, which is stubbed on this build.
payload_formats.zone_audio_state: The extended per-zone audio state blocks: the status records the player keeps for each zone's audio, covering volume, EQ, and queue-related flags beyond the headline values.
payload_formats.SonosAvtStateFile: The vocabulary of names used in the transport's save and restore machinery: the keys the player writes when it persists playback state so it can resume after a reboot.
payload_formats.status_doc: The complete element grammar of the diagnostics pages: every field the built-in status website can emit, so the diagnostics surface is fully documented rather than just its route list.
payload_formats.sonos_diag_filename: The diagnostic filename pattern: IP address plus date and time baked into the name, so a diagnostics bundle names which machine and moment it came from at a glance.
payload_formats.fixed_volume_tokens: 'FV' markers and related tokens the tone machinery parses for fixed-volume handling: the small vocabulary inside the extended-EQ router that decides when volume stays locked.
payload_formats.sonos_favorites_version: The 'FV:' version token: a marker used in two different places, inside the EQ parameter machinery and as a favorites-list version. It's documented separately so the same-looking token isn't misread.
payload_formats.contentdir_root_map: The top of the music library tree: the fixed root containers every browse starts from, including artists, albums, tracks, genres, playlists, and folders, recovered from the enumeration code.
payload_formats.sonos_metadata_urn: The metadata URN for content ratings: the namespace tag marking rating metadata inside track descriptions so rating fields get recognized.
payload_formats.sonos_packed_object_id: This token captures what another speaker needs to take over playback: the track ordinal, byte position in the audio stream, packet cursor and playback timing, seek target, and group capabilities. Its last64 characters carry the audio-framer bookmark. The worker finishes the snapshot before it is serialized. A cloning flag can preserve the existing transmitter cursor instead of resetting it. Parsing can leave partial changes on failure, so callers must check its result.
payload_formats.sonos_hex_blob_line: This is a playback bookmark that lets the speaker recover where it was in an audio stream. For HLS it remembers the bitrate, which stream was selected, and the segment sequence. It travels with a separate byte offset. The parser accepts optional sections and trailing text, and a failed parse can leave partial data behind; callers must check its result.
payload_formats.sonos_mac_parse: How the player reads a MAC address: the six-hex-pairs-with-colons shape it accepts for hardware identifiers, parsed strictly so malformed addresses are rejected.
payload_formats.sonos_mac_dash: A MAC-address variant using dashes instead of colons: the second accepted hardware-address shape, so both common spellings parse.
payload_formats.sonos_version_pair: How version numbers are written: 'major.minor' pairs like 86.10, which is the shape the firmware's version comparisons and update checks accept.
payload_formats.sonos_https_ep: The secure-endpoint address pattern: 'https://' plus IP and port, which is how a direct secure endpoint is written when the player names one.
payload_formats.sonos_http_statusline: How the player reads an HTTP status line: the 'HTTP/1.1 200' shape its own HTTP client and server machinery parses.
payload_formats.sonos_http_date_emit: How the player writes HTTP Date headers: the single canonical date format it emits when dating its own responses.
payload_formats.sonos_path_two_seg: A two-segment path split: the 'first/second' grammar used where a route or locator is divided into exactly two parts.
payload_formats.sonos_iv_token: An 'IV=' prefixed token the firmware scans for: an initialization-vector style field seen where encrypted data is handled.
payload_formats.sonos_buzzer_uri: The file paths of the built-in alarm buzzers: where the speaker's own software keeps its wake-up tones. These files live inside the device's storage and aren't something you can browse to or change.
payload_formats.itunes_plist_importer: The vocabulary of the iTunes-library importer: the keys the player recognizes when importing an iTunes XML playlist file. It's the bridge that lets an iTunes library become a Sonos library.
payload_formats.sonos_class_audioBook: The object class for audiobook items: the tag marking a library item as an audiobook rather than music, so apps can shelve it correctly.
payload_formats.vli_mimes: The content types a virtual line-in session accepts: the whitelist of formats an external source may push at the player.
payload_formats.ncd_device_payload: The factory-default configuration blob: the template of non-volatile config data programmed into each unit at manufacture, found embedded in the firmware as a payload.
payload_formats.http_status_map: The player's HTTP status-code tables: two parallel maps translating internal results into web status codes, covering the extended set of statuses its web layer can emit.
payload_formats.smapi_capability_bits: The capability bitfield for music-service integrations: the packed flags word where each bit declares a feature a service supports (seeking, skipping, metadata kinds), decoded bit by bit.
payload_formats.transport_action_bits: The packed transport-actions field: how the 'currently legal commands' answer is encoded as bits, and which bit means play, pause, seek, and the rest.
payload_formats.skip_restriction_bits: The packed skip-restriction flags: the bits describing what a source forbids (no next, no previous), used when a service constrains navigation.
payload_formats.codec_mime_flags: The decoder and format flag packing: how audio-format capabilities are encoded as bit flags alongside their MIME descriptions.

state_variables.AVT.TransportState: The headline playback state: PLAYING, PAUSED_PLAYBACK, STOPPED, or TRANSITIONING. It is the single most-watched variable on the player, because every 'is it playing?' answer in every app comes from this one field.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentTrackMetaData: The metadata for the playing track: title, artist, album, and artwork, packed in the track-metadata XML format. Everything the app's now-playing display shows about the song comes from this field.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentTrackURI: The address of the playing track itself, meaning the specific item's URI. It is distinct from the source-level AVTransportURI: the queue might be the source while this names the exact song inside it.
state_variables.AVT.AVTransportURI: The address of what's loaded in the player right now: a queue reference, a radio stream URL, a line-in selector, or a service item. When this value changes, the speaker is pointing at something different, so it is effectively the answer to 'what is this room set to play'.
state_variables.AVT.r:EnqueuedTransportURI: The address of the source queued up to take over, meaning the next program's URI. It names what will become current when the player switches source, which is distinct from the next track inside the current program.
state_variables.AVT.TransportStatus: The health of the transport: OK or an error indicator. It is paired with the state so 'stopped because you asked' can be told apart from 'stopped because the stream died'.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentTransportActions: The list of transport commands currently legal, such as 'Play,Stop,Next', computed live from the source and state. Apps read it to decide which buttons to enable and which to grey out.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentPlayMode: The current play mode: normal, repeat-all, repeat-one, shuffle, or shuffle-and-repeat. It is the variable behind which shuffle and repeat icons light up in the app.
state_variables.AVT.NumberOfTracks: How many tracks are in the current program. For queue playback this is the queue length, and for sources that behave like lists it reports whatever count the source provides.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentTrack: The index of the track currently playing, meaning which entry of the queue is live right now. It advances as the queue progresses, and combined with NumberOfTracks it produces 'track 4 of 23'.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentTrackDuration: How long the current track is. This is the value the app's progress bar divides elapsed time by to draw its fill position.
state_variables.AVT.TransportErrorHttpCode: When a stream fails, this holds the HTTP status from the failed fetch, for example a 404 from a dead stream URL. It lets apps tell 'the file is gone' apart from 'the network died'.
state_variables.AVT.r:DirectControlClientID: Which client owns an active direct-control session, meaning the specific app or instance behind an external feed. It is set while a direct-control session owns the player.
state_variables.AVT.r:SleepTimerGeneration: A counter that ticks whenever the sleep timer is set, changed, or cancelled. It lets apps tell a fresh timer apart from an old one without comparing durations.
state_variables.AVT.r:AlarmRunning: Whether an alarm is currently ringing. It is set while an alarm fires so the system (and the snooze and stop logic) knows an alarm session is live. The 'r:' prefix marks it as a Sonos extension beyond the standard variable set.
state_variables.AVT.r:SnoozeRunning: Whether an alarm snooze is currently counting down. It is set between hitting snooze and the alarm re-ringing, which is how the system knows a snooze is in progress.
state_variables.RCS.Volume: The volume per channel, which is the most-watched variable on this service. Every slider move, button press, or remote command lands here.
state_variables.RCS.Mute: The mute flag per channel, the most basic evented variable on this service. It fires every time mute flips, whether the change came from an app or the physical button.
state_variables.RCS.Bass: The bass level. It is the equalizer's bass setting, evented so the app's EQ panel tracks changes made anywhere in the system.
state_variables.RCS.Treble: The treble level. It is the equalizer's treble setting, evented alongside bass so every view reflects the new value as soon as it changes anywhere.
state_variables.RCS.Loudness: The loudness toggle. Loudness is Sonos's fullness boost for quiet listening, and it is evented alongside the rest of the EQ state.
state_variables.RCS.NightMode: Whether night mode is on. Night mode is the dynamic-range compressor that softens loud effects for late-night TV, reported here as a home-theater toggle.
state_variables.RCS.DialogLevel: The dialogue-boost amount: how much speech-enhancement lift is applied on products that offer it. It is a per-model tone control for making voices easier to hear.
state_variables.RCS.SubGain: The subwoofer gain, meaning the sub's level trim relative to the rest of the rig. In plain terms, it controls how hot the bass runs.
state_variables.RCS.SurroundLevel: The surround speakers' level trim, controlling how loud the rear speakers play relative to the soundbar.
state_variables.RCS.SurroundEnabled: Whether surround speakers are active in the rig. It is the rear-channel enable flag inside a bonded theater setup, toggling the rears' participation on or off.
state_variables.RCS.AudioDelay: The lip-sync delay for the main output: how much audio delay is applied so sound lines up with the TV picture. It exists because video processing adds latency the audio must wait out.
state_variables.RCS.SonarEnabled: Whether sonar calibration is currently enabled, which is the tuning system's on/off state after a completed calibration.
state_variables.RCS.PresetNameList: The list of named EQ and volume presets available. It is the preset vocabulary some products expose for one-tap sound modes.
state_variables.CD.FavoritesUpdateID: A version counter for the favorites list. It bumps whenever your saved stations, playlists, or items change, which tells apps their favorites view is stale.
state_variables.CD.RadioFavoritesUpdateID: A version counter for saved radio favorites. It bumps when your radio presets change, so the stations list refreshes only when it needs to.
state_variables.CD.SavedQueuesUpdateID: A version counter for Sonos playlists. It bumps when any saved queue is created, edited, or deleted, making it the 'your playlists changed' signal.
state_variables.CD.ShareListUpdateID: A version counter for the music-shares list. It bumps when folders are added to or removed from the library, so apps re-fetch the share list only when it changed.
state_variables.CD.ShareIndexInProgress: Whether a music-library rescan is running right now. It is the flag behind the 'updating music index' spinner, on while a rescan walks your folders.
state_variables.CD.ContainerUpdateIDs: The change-markers for library containers: a list of which folders and playlists changed since the last check. It lets an app refresh only the parts of its browse view that moved instead of re-reading the whole library.
state_variables.GRC.GroupVolume: The group's aggregate volume, which is the number behind the group slider. The coordinator re-derives it as member levels change.
state_variables.GRC.GroupMute: The group's mute state. It is the evented flag every controller follows for the group mute button, so when it changes anywhere, every app sees it flip.
state_variables.GRC.GroupVolumeChangeable: Whether the group volume can currently be changed. In some configurations the group level is locked or derived, and this flag tells the app the slider should be disabled.
state_variables.Queue.QueueID: The identifier of the queue being described, naming which managed queue an event or answer refers to.
state_variables.Queue.UpdateID: A queue's version stamp. It bumps on every edit, and apps send it back to prove they're editing the version they last saw, which prevents lost updates.
state_variables.Queue.Curated: Whether a queue is 'curated', meaning marked as managed by some system component rather than a raw user queue.
state_variables.GM.LocalGroupUUID: The identifier of the group this speaker currently belongs to. It is its group membership expressed in one value, and it changes on every group and ungroup.
state_variables.GM.DelegatedGroupCoordinatorID: Which member group leadership was delegated to. It is set during a coordinator hand-off so the topology knows who is taking over the group.
state_variables.GM.VirtualLineInGroupID: The group associated with a virtual line-in session. It is set while an external feed session exists, tying the session to the group it serves.
state_variables.ZGT.ZoneGroupState: The entire household map as one variable: every player, its room name, its group, and each group's leader, packed into a single document. It is the heartbeat of multi-room awareness, because it changes and announces every time the system's shape changes.
state_variables.DP.CurrentZoneName: This speaker's room name, the label you gave it in the app such as 'Kitchen'. It fires when the room gets renamed, so every display updates.
state_variables.DP.MicEnabled: Whether the speaker's microphone is enabled. It is the mic-on flag for voice-capable products, kept in this service's spec for parity even though this older hardware has no mic.
state_variables.DP.Invisible: Whether the speaker is hidden. This 'invisible' flag removes the player from normal room display, and it is used for satellites and bonded members that shouldn't appear as separate rooms.
state_variables.AC.AlarmListVersion: A version counter for the alarm list that ticks up every time an alarm is created, edited, or deleted. Apps watch this single number to know their cached alarm list went stale instead of re-fetching the whole list constantly.
state_variables.AC.TimeServer: The address of the network time source the speaker syncs against. It reports where the household clock comes from so apps and diagnostics can see the configured time server.
state_variables.MS.ServiceListVersion: A version counter for the music-service catalog. It bumps when the available-services list changes, so apps re-pull the catalog only when it moved.
state_variables.HT.RemoteConfigured: Whether the speaker has a configured infrared remote. It is set once remote-learning is done, and it is the flag apps check before offering the setup wizard.
state_variables.HT.LEDFeedbackState: Whether the remote-received LED flash is on. It is the home-theater feedback setting, evented so settings screens stay truthful about the device state.
state_variables.AI.TOSLinkConnected: Whether something is plugged into the optical input, which is the line-in detection flag. It is part of the AudioIn surface that is a reject-everything stub on this firmware.
state_variables.AI.IRRepeaterState: Whether the infrared repeater is currently on. It mirrors the home-theater IR setting so a change shows up as an event, though it is dead on this build along with the rest of the AudioIn surface.
state_variables.RCS.OutputFixed: Whether output is fixed-level. It is the flag that locks the speaker at line level for feeding an external amplifier.
state_variables.RCS.SpeakerSize: The speaker-size classification: the large/small designation the audio pipeline uses for bass handling in home-theater configuration.
state_variables.RCS.SubCrossover: The subwoofer crossover frequency: where bass hands off from the soundbar to the bonded sub. It is one of the home-theater tuning values.
state_variables.RCS.SubPolarity: The subwoofer polarity: the phase setting (normal or inverted) that keeps the sub's bass in step with the bar's drivers.
state_variables.RCS.SubEnabled: Whether the bonded subwoofer is enabled. It is the variable behind the app switch for 'use the sub', toggling the sub's participation in the theater rig.
state_variables.RCS.SpeechEnhanceEnabled: Whether speech enhancement is on. It is the dialogue-clarity feature on theater products, evented so the app's toggle follows the real device state.
state_variables.RCS.SupportsMaxDialogLevel: Whether this device supports the maximum dialogue-level setting. It is a capability flag that gates the strongest speech-boost option.
state_variables.RCS.MusicSurroundLevel: How much music playback goes to the surround speakers. It is the 'ambient versus full' music-surround level in a home-theater setup.
state_variables.RCS.AudioDelayLeftRear: Lip-sync delay for the left rear channel. It is the surround-specific version of the audio delay, letting the left rear be timed independently.
state_variables.RCS.AudioDelayRightRear: Lip-sync delay for the right rear channel, the companion to the left-rear delay. It gives the right rear its own lip-sync trim.
state_variables.RCS.SurroundMode: The surround mode for music playback: the 'ambient' versus 'full' setting that decides how much music goes to the rear speakers.
state_variables.RCS.HeightChannelLevel: The level of height or ceiling channels. It is a setting for surround products with upward-firing speakers, present here only for spec parity on this older unit.
state_variables.RCS.SonarCalibrationAvailable: Whether sonar or room calibration can run on this device. It is a capability flag telling apps whether to offer the tuning feature.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentCrossfadeMode: Whether crossfade is on. It is the blend-between-tracks setting, reported so the app's toggle stays in sync with the actual player state.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentSection: Which 'section' of the current program is active. It is used by sources with internal structure like chapters or segments, and for ordinary tracks it effectively means the current position in the list.
state_variables.AVT.r:EnqueuedTransportURIMetaData: The description of whatever EnqueuedTransportURI points at. It lets apps show what's coming next at the program level rather than the track level.
state_variables.AVT.PlaybackStorageMedium: Which 'medium' the current playback comes from: queue, network stream, line-in, and so on. It is the broad category label for the current source.
state_variables.AVT.AVTransportURIMetaData: The description of what's loaded: title, artwork, and other display metadata for whatever AVTransportURI points at. It is packed in the track-metadata format that apps render the 'now playing' header from.
state_variables.AVT.NextAVTransportURI: The address of the next track, announced in advance. It is the gapless-playback lookahead: what has been lined up to play when the current track ends, so the player can pre-buffer it.
state_variables.AVT.NextAVTransportURIMetaData: The metadata for the announced next track, meaning the title and artwork the app can show in 'up next' before the track actually starts.
state_variables.AVT.r:CurrentValidPlayModes: Which play modes are currently legal: the shuffle and repeat choices you may pick right now, computed from the source. Repeat-one makes no sense on a live stream, so it is omitted then.
state_variables.AVT.r:DirectControlIsSuspended: Whether the direct-control session is suspended: paused in a way that keeps the session alive while the external source isn't actively streaming.
state_variables.AVT.r:DirectControlAccountID: Which account owns an active direct-control session. It is the identity of the external service feeding the player, set while one is in control.
state_variables.AVT.TransportErrorDescription: A text description of the last transport failure: the human-readable message attached when playback errors, describing what went wrong.
state_variables.AVT.TransportErrorURI: The address that failed when a transport error occurred. It identifies which stream or item the error belongs to, so the failure can be traced back to its source.
state_variables.AVT.TransportErrorHttpHeaders: The response headers captured from a failed stream fetch. They are extra diagnostics attached to transport errors, useful for debugging why a stream died.
state_variables.AVT.r:RestartPending: Whether the player has flagged that a restart is pending. It is a marker used around updates and recovery so clients know the session may bounce.
state_variables.AVT.r:NextTrackURI: The next track's address in the Sonos extension namespace. It is the same lookahead concept as NextAVTransportURI, exposed under the r: prefix.
state_variables.AVT.r:NextTrackMetaData: The metadata for the next track in the Sonos extension namespace. It parallels the standard NextAVTransportURIMetaData under the r: prefix.
state_variables.AVT.TransportPlaySpeed: The playback speed, normally '1'. It is the standard's field for variable-speed playback, which this firmware doesn't implement.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentMediaDuration: The total duration of the loaded media. It is pinned at 'not implemented' in this build because Sonos reports durations per-track through CurrentTrackDuration rather than for the whole program.
state_variables.AVT.RecordStorageMedium: Which medium would be recorded to. It is fixed at none on a playback-only device, included as spec boilerplate.
state_variables.AVT.PossiblePlaybackStorageMedia: The list of source types this player can play: the hardware's declared talents, fixed per model, describing which media categories it will accept at all.
state_variables.AVT.PossibleRecordStorageMedia: The recording media the player claims. The answer is none, and it is another spec field kept for completeness on a device that doesn't record.
state_variables.AVT.RecordMediumWriteStatus: Write-protect status of the 'record medium'. It is boilerplate for a player that doesn't record, present because the standard requires the field.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentRecordQualityMode: The recording quality setting. It is a leftover field from the standard spec, permanently 'not implemented' on a speaker that doesn't record.
state_variables.AVT.PossibleRecordQualityModes: The recording-quality options the player claims. The answer is none, since a speaker doesn't record, and it is standard-spec boilerplate kept for protocol completeness.
state_variables.Queue.QueueOwnerID: Which component owns a queue: the entity (an internal module or a session) holding edit rights over it.
state_variables.AC.TimeFormat: The speaker's preferred clock format: 12-hour versus 24-hour. It is read by anything displaying times the way the speaker was configured to.
state_variables.AC.TimeGeneration: A counter that bumps whenever the household clock settings change, covering timezone switches, manual time sets, and server changes. It lets other devices notice 'the clock just moved' and react.
state_variables.AC.DateFormat: The speaker's preferred date display format. It is the setting behind how dates render in anything that asks the player rather than guessing at your region's convention.
state_variables.CM.CurrentConnectionIDs: The list of live connections against the player, which is the evented form of the connection-list command. It fires whenever a control session opens or closes.
state_variables.DP.ResetVolumeAfter: Whether the speaker resets its volume after a triggered session. It is the flag used by alarm and autoplay so a wake-up volume doesn't become the permanent level.
state_variables.renderingcontrol_status_schema: The fields on the diagnostics page for the volume and tone service. It is the player's internal view of channel volumes, mutes, EQ values, and flags, exposed for support and debugging.
state_variables.playstatemanager_schema: The fields of the play-state manager page on the diagnostics site. It is the component's own view of who's playing what where, exposed for debugging group playback issues.
state_variables.alarm_status_schema: The field list for the alarm page on the player's built-in diagnostics website: which alarm details the player exposes when you or support tools visit its status pages, covering what's scheduled, what's ringing, and the bookkeeping around each.
state_variables.zone_group_state_schema: The layout of the household-map document, which is the same ZoneGroupState the topology service emits: every player, room, group, and coordinator, structured so any device can parse the whole system's shape.
state_variables.zoneplayers_status_schema: The fields of the ZonePlayers diagnostics page: the player's internal census of every speaker it knows about, including IDs, rooms, versions, and addresses, exposed for debugging.
state_variables.device_props_update_ids: The set of change-counters the device-properties service keeps. These version numbers tick when different aspects of the speaker's config change, so interested parties can tell what moved without comparing every field.
state_variables.update_info_schema: The fields of the update-info diagnostics page: what the player reports about its firmware status, covering current version, what updates are pending or downloading, and update history.
state_variables.sounddevice_status_schema: The fields of the SoundDevice diagnostics page, which is per-zone audio bookkeeping: each player's volume, ducking state, and output details as the player reports them internally.
state_variables.replicated_netsettings_schema: The layout of the replicated network-settings document exchanged between players. It is the shared network config (including WiFi details) every household member keeps in sync, so any player can stand up the same network configuration.
state_variables.vli_state_snapshot: The snapshot recorded when a virtual line-in session changes state: the fields captured at transitions so the session can be handed off or resumed, covering source, coordinator, and transport settings at that moment.
state_variables.shares_schema: The layout of the replicated share registry: the document listing your music-library folders that all household players keep a copy of, so every speaker can index and play from the same shares.
state_variables.device_props_extra_vars: Additional device-property fields the settings service carries beyond the standard set: the extra bits of speaker configuration reported alongside the usual name, LED, and button state.
state_variables.savedqueues_rsq_schema: The file format of the saved-queues store on disk, meaning how Sonos playlists are actually persisted on the speaker. It is the record structure that survives reboots, written by the queue-backup commands.
state_variables.services_xml_schema: The layout of the replicated services list: the document describing which music services exist on the household that all players share, so every speaker sees the same service catalog.
state_variables.userradio_schema: The layout of the user-radio favorites file: the document storing your saved radio stations, plus the delta-file format used to apply incremental changes without rewriting the whole list.
state_variables.zpinfo_schema: The layout of the player's self-description documents: the fields a speaker publishes about itself, covering identity, device info, and play-mode capabilities, used by the rest of the household to recognize it.
state_variables.netsettings_schema: The layout of the player's replicated network-settings store: the on-disk document holding WiFi credentials and network configuration that all devices in the household share. This is where your WiFi password actually lives inside the system: encrypted per-household and replicated across players so any of them can join the network.
state_variables.avt_lastchange: The field list for the transport service's bundled change reports: everything packed into the 'what just changed in playback' message, covering state, track, position, mode, and source. One event carries all of this at once, which is why an app updates its whole now-playing screen from a single notification.
state_variables.zp_support_info: The layout of the support-information bundle: the structured data gathered when you submit diagnostics, covering versions, hardware details, state, and configuration, packaged so Sonos support can read it.
state_variables.zps_page: The fields of the household update-status page: the diagnostics view showing each player's update state during a rollout, covering who's updated, who's downloading, and who's pending or failed.
state_variables.ht_input_session: The telemetry fields captured for a home-theater input session: the bookkeeping the soundbar keeps about an active TV or optical input session, covering source, timing, and session state.

muse_resources.alarms: Alarm management for the modern API, which is the JSON twin of the classic alarm service covered on the service pages. Everything the app's alarm screen does flows through these routes: listing every alarm the household knows about, creating a new one with its time, sound, and room, editing an existing alarm's fields, and deleting alarms you no longer want. Where the classic commands work one alarm at a time through verbose message exchanges, this surface treats alarms as ordinary API objects an app can fetch and edit like any other data.
muse_resources.areas: Household 'areas', the multi-room spaces concept newer app versions use to organize a home into named zones beyond plain rooms. An area groups players into a logical space like 'downstairs', and these routes let an app list the household's areas and manage which players belong to each. It's part of the newer organizational model the app is migrating toward.
muse_resources.audioClip: The audio-clip feature: short sounds the system can play over whatever else is going on, like a doorbell chime ringing through every speaker, an intercom-style announcement, or a system alert tone. These routes cover uploading a clip into the household and triggering it to play, so a smart doorbell or home-automation event can make the speakers speak.
muse_resources.authorization: The sign-in and credential surface for the modern API, where API keys and authorization tokens are issued, presented, and checked. Every other resource group in the modern API trusts the credentials established here, so this is the foundation under the whole security model: get a valid credential here first, or nothing else will talk to you.
muse_resources.catalog: The music catalog surface: browsable service content (a service's playlists, charts, stations, and directories) exposed to the app as API resources. It bridges the old browse-the-catalog model into the modern JSON interface, so apps can walk a service's content tree through the same kind of calls they use for everything else.
muse_resources.devices: The device list: every player in the household presented as a modern API object with its identity, model, capabilities, and current state. When the app builds its roster of 'your Sonos products', this is where that data comes from, with one resource per physical speaker.
muse_resources.devicesExtended: The extended device surface: the deeper per-device detail beyond the basics, including richer capability flags, configuration state, and diagnostics-grade fields the plain devices list doesn't carry. Apps needing more than a name and model consult this instead.
muse_resources.diagnostics: Diagnostics over the modern API: triggering log collection, fetching diagnostic state, and driving the support-reporting flow as JSON routes rather than through the old diagnostic web pages. When the app files a diagnostic report, this is the surface it uses.
muse_resources.effectiveSettings: Settings as the speaker actually applies them: the resolved result after defaults, household values, group values, and device-level overrides are merged into one answer. Reading 'the setting' here gives the value that governs real behavior rather than what some screen last typed, which is why automation and the app prefer this surface for checking current state.
muse_resources.entitlements: Which features this household is entitled to: the license and entitlement surface telling the system (and the app) which capabilities are unlocked, covering subscriptions, feature flags, and regional eligibility. It's the gatekeeping data behind 'this feature isn't available on your system'.
muse_resources.favorites: The favorites list over the modern API: your saved stations, playlists, and items managed as plain API resources, covering listing what's saved, adding new favorites, and removing old ones. It's the JSON counterpart of the favorites the classic library service tracks.
muse_resources.groupVolume: Group-level volume over the modern API: the JSON version of the group volume and mute commands, covering setting the group's absolute level, adjusting it by a step, and reading the aggregate value. These are the routes behind the app's single slider that moves every grouped room at once.
muse_resources.groups: Group management for the modern API: creating groups from rooms, adding member players, removing them, and dissolving groups back into independent rooms. These are the routes behind 'group rooms' in the app.
muse_resources.hardwareStatus: Hardware health and status: the player's report on its physical state, covering temperatures, wireless link quality, and other machine-level readings. Diagnostics screens and the network-health features draw from these routes to explain what's happening inside the box.
muse_resources.hdmi: The HDMI input surface: controlling and reading the TV-connected input on products with HDMI-ARC, covering audio mode, TV detection, format, and the settings around how the soundbar takes its TV feed. It's relevant to the soundbar-era products this codebase serves.
muse_resources.history: Playback history: what this player has played recently, exposed as an API resource. Features that show your listening history (or that report it) draw their data from these routes.
muse_resources.homeTheater: The home-theater settings surface: everything specific to a TV-connected rig over the modern API, covering lip-sync delay, surround levels, subwoofer settings, night mode, and speech enhancement. It's the JSON surface behind the 'home theater' section of the soundbar's settings.
muse_resources.householdUpdate: Household firmware updates over the modern API: checking whether updates exist, reading the rollout status per player, and triggering the update process, all as JSON routes. The current app's 'update your system' flow runs through here.
muse_resources.households: The household resource itself: the top-level object all household-scoped routes hang off, which is the umbrella identity under which players, groups, and services live. A request naming a household says 'this operation is about the system as a whole, not one speaker'.
muse_resources.info: General player information: version, model, identity, and related facts. It's the modern API's 'about this device' read, used by anything needing the player's basic description.
muse_resources.ircontrol: Infrared remote control over the modern API: the remote-learning and IR-repeater features expressed as routes. It's the modern twin of the classic home-theater control commands that teach the soundbar your TV remote.
muse_resources.localContentLibrary: The local music library over the modern API: your indexed share folders, their contents, and library maintenance exposed as JSON resources. It's the modern front-end for the same library the classic browse service serves, so the app can manage 'Music Library' without the old protocol.
muse_resources.management: Device management: reboot, factory-reset paths, and similarly powerful maintenance operations over the modern API. These are deliberately restricted, since they're the routes you don't want a random network client reaching, which is part of why the API authenticates every call.
muse_resources.musicServiceAccounts: Streaming-service accounts over the modern API: the JSON version of the account-management family, covering adding a service login, replacing credentials, setting a nickname, and removing an account. These are the routes behind the app's service account settings.
muse_resources.networkTest: Network testing: routes that exercise the player's connectivity, including ping-style checks and throughput probes. Diagnostics and the app's network-health features use them to prove whether the player's connection is the problem.
muse_resources.pinewood: An internal codename surface: the 'pinewood' routes cover a feature family known in the firmware by its development name (a remote-control channel in this case). It's structurally present, and the operations below show exactly which routes it exposes.
muse_resources.platformInternal: Internal platform routes: operations meant for Sonos's own components rather than apps. It's the back-channel surface of the modern API, used for system-level coordination between the player's own parts and Sonos's services.
muse_resources.playback: Playback control over the modern API: the core remote of play, pause, skip, seek, and source selection expressed as JSON commands. This is the surface the current app actually drives when you press buttons on the now-playing screen, the modern counterpart of the classic transport commands.
muse_resources.playbackExtended: Extended playback operations: the less-common transport actions beyond basic play/pause, covering session control, source management, and the richer playback verbs the main playback group doesn't carry.
muse_resources.playbackMetadata: Now-playing metadata over the modern API: the current track's title, artist, album, artwork, and related display data as a resource the app can fetch cleanly, rather than parsing it out of the packed metadata strings the classic layer uses.
muse_resources.playbackSession: Playback sessions: the modern API's model of 'a thing playing'. It tracks a session's lifecycle from creation through playing, suspension, and end, letting the app reason about playback as objects with state rather than reading raw variables.
muse_resources.playerVolume: Per-player volume over the modern API: a single speaker's volume and mute as JSON resources. It's the modern twin of the classic rendering-control commands, behind the per-room sliders.
muse_resources.playlists: Sonos playlists over the modern API: the saved-queue feature as resources, covering listing the playlists stored on the system, creating new ones, editing their contents, and deleting them. It's the JSON surface behind 'Sonos Playlists' in the app.
muse_resources.positioning: Speaker positioning: the room-placement features, covering which physical spot a speaker occupies in a bonded or surround arrangement and the operations for assigning and detecting those positions during setup.
muse_resources.power: Standby and sleep behavior plus power-state reads over the modern API. It's the modern counterpart of the standby and idle machinery, and it's how the app asks about and controls the player's power state directly.
muse_resources.roomDetection: Room detection over the modern API: the 'which physical speaker is this' identification feature as routes. It's the chirp-and-identify flow used while placing surrounds and bonded speakers.
muse_resources.settings: General settings over the modern API: the player's configuration as readable and writable JSON settings rather than one command per knob. It's the consolidated settings surface the app prefers.
muse_resources.sleepTimer: The sleep timer over the modern API: set a 'stop playing in N minutes' timer, read how much is left, and cancel it. It's a small resource group mirroring the classic sleep-timer commands.
muse_resources.smartplay: 'Smart play', Sonos's smarter playback-decision feature family, exposed as its own resource group. The operations listed below are the routes it adds, and the name reflects an intelligent-playback feature rather than a user-facing setting.
muse_resources.soundSwap: Sound swap: the feature that moves a TV's audio between a soundbar and a paired portable speaker ('swap the sound to the other room'), exposed as API routes for triggering and managing the swap.
muse_resources.svc: An internal service-level group: routes that don't fit a named resource, used for operations scoped to the API itself rather than to a thing like 'playback' or 'alarms'.
muse_resources.systemReporting: System reporting: fleet-level telemetry and reporting routes, covering how the player packages and sends its health and usage data to Sonos over the modern channel.
